newsitem.title: FRANCE: AXA says offer for UAP looks successful.
newsitem.headline: AXA says offer for UAP looks successful.

text.p: Insurer Axa said on Wednesday that its exchange offer for UAP shares that closes today appeared to have been very successful.
"The results will be published on January 13, 1997, but it is widely acknowledged to have been very successful," Axa said in a statement.
The agreement creates the world's second largest insurer, with annual premium income of more than 300 billion francs.

As previously announced, the new holding firm will have a supervisory board and an executive board. The supervisory board will appoint the executive board and oversee group management. The executive board assisted by an executive committee will be responsible for managing the group.
It will be proposed that UAP chairman Jacques Friednmann be appointed chairman of the supervisory board and Jean-Pierre Ruault, the group's corporate secretary, act as its secretary.

Axa chairman Claude Bebear is to be chairman of the executive board of the holding, making him effectively chief executive officer. Including Bebear, the board is to be made up six members from UAP and 10 from Axa.

While Axa insisted when the deal was announced it was "a friendly operation between equals," analysts said they had little doubt highly profitable Axa would dominate larger, formerly state-owned UAP, which recently returned to profit.
"What counted for us (in forming the executive committee) was competence and experience in insurance as well as internationally," said an Axa spokeswoman.
"We really don't care about which company the people came from. What matters to us is competence," she said.
She said that eight of the 16 executive committee members were from abroad, reflecting the new group's stress on developing its international activities.

Those named to the board, who will be senior executive vice presidents of the new group, include Dominique Bazy, chairman of UAP France, Jim Benson, chief executive officer of Axa's U.S. unit Equitable Life, Henri de Castries, Axa executive vice president and Geoff Tomlinson, managing director of Axa's National Mutual in Australia.

The committee will meet once every six weeks to oversee the group's strategic and financial orientations. The Axa spokeswoman said that members of the supervisory committee which will meet three times a year to discuss the group's long term strategy will be appointed soon.

On January 22, a meeting of Axa shareholders will be held in order to issue the Axa shares and certificates of guaranteed value that will be allotted to UAP shareholders in the deal valued at 40 billion francs. On May 12, a merger between the two holding companies will be proposed to shareholders of the two groups in separate meetings.
